what_happened: In job vesh, the user corrected Athena's first reading before work began. The job adds an import step that runs at a cutover job's landing and writes a legacy-exempt record. The reading missed that vesh itself is landed by the Athena built before it, and that build does not run the import. The user added a catch-up. When the job named by cutover_job has a landing record on athena/records but no import commit exists, the reconcile step at the start of `athena land` and `athena status` runs the import at C0 and writes the legacy-exempt record once. A second run writes nothing. The user also asked for a test of that path. The rest of the reading stood.
cause: The reading stage works from the request text and has no step asking which build lands the job. When a job changes Athena's own landing behavior, the change is not live at its own landing, so a one-time action tied to that landing never happens. Nothing makes the reading name this bootstrap gap or require an idempotent catch-up for the already-landed case. This differs from the stale-binary case (6sq5), which is about setup not being re-run. Here the ordering is inherent to self-landing.
prevention: Add a required reading step for any job that changes Athena's own landing, reconcile or import behavior. The reading must state which build lands the job and whether the new behavior will run at that landing. If it will not, the reading must include an idempotent catch-up in the reconcile step that runs on `athena land` and `athena status`. It must also include a test of the already-landed-but-not-imported state and a test that a second run writes nothing. The critic should refuse a reading that has a landing-time action but no such catch-up.
proposed_request: Add the legacy import for the cutover job named by cutover_job. The import runs at C0 and writes one legacy-exempt record. This job is landed by the Athena built before it, which does not run the import. So add a catch-up to the reconcile step at the start of `athena land` and `athena status`. When the cutover job has a landing record on athena/records but no import commit exists yet, the catch-up runs the import at C0 and writes the legacy-exempt record once. It must be idempotent, so a second run writes nothing. Acceptance: (1) a test where the cutover landing exists and no import commit exists, which shows the import and the record are written once; (2) a test that a second run writes nothing; (3) a test that the normal landing path still runs the import and writes the record once. Keep the rest of the earlier reading unchanged.
